notes.title: [ENG/ES] How we create our environments? / ¿Cómo creamos nuestros escenarios?
notes.notes:
¡Versión en español mas abajo!

[b][English version][/b]

Some time ago we announced the second map for Deck RX - [b]The WasteSands [/b]- and as we are getting closer to the date when we will include it in the ODB (Open Dev Access) builds, we are polishing some details!

This map has already been played by some players in the events we attended during last months of 2022, but now we have been changing some details here and there, mostly of its background, to make it stand out during the race without annoy the player.

This is what The WasteSands previously looked like.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/4270a6b1f975ab0ac4a497c91bfca5a4b09da3f5.png[/img]

The distance between camera and background landscapes in [b]Deck RX [/b]forces us to develope very detailed environments or better said, environments full of elements and decorations to avoid them looking too empty.

This is a[b] challenging task [/b]as we have to find the perfect balance to give the game a smooth performance without losing any graphic quality.

In this new WasteSands we have managed to reduce the amount of polygons from 2 million to only half a million.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/89e676d33ad59e82e6470db44b426ac0d9eb31c9.png[/img]

Also, as an extra, we share some screenshots of what the map would look like without color, so that those more interested can visualize the geometry of the mesh we use :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/ea66e1bab9049b1a6d6c935a4fdd98f65e1ca0e6.png[/img]

Soon you will have more news about the development of [b]Deck RX[/b]! Remember to wishlist it[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1529180/Deck_RX_The_Deckbuilding_Racing_Game/] here[/url] and tell-a-friend if you think they might be interested! That helps us a lot to reach more people!

See you soon!

=============================================================

[Spanish version]

Hace un tiempo os anunciamos cuál sería el segundo mapa de Deck RX - [b]The WasteSands [/b]- y como ya se acerca la fecha en la que lo incluiremos en las builds de ODB (Open Dev Access) estamos ultimando los detalles!

Este mapa ya ha sido jugado por algunos jugadores en los eventos a los que asistimos durante el pasado otoño de 2022, pero ahora hemos estado retocando y ultimando los detalles de su fondo para que destaque sin llegar a molestar, al igual que añadiéndole algunos pequeños detalles.

Así era como se veía anteriormente [b]The WasteSands[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/4270a6b1f975ab0ac4a497c91bfca5a4b09da3f5.png[/img]

La distancia a la que se encuentran los paisajes de fondo en [b]Deck RX[/b] nos obliga a crear entornos muy detallados o mejor dicho, entornos cargados de elementos y decoraciones para evitar que parezcan demasiado vacíos. Esto es un reto, ya que hay que encontrar el balance perfecto de cara al rendimiento sin sacrificar el aspecto visual. En el nuevo WasteSands hemos conseguido rebajar la cantidad de polígonos de 2 millones a tan solo medio millón.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/89e676d33ad59e82e6470db44b426ac0d9eb31c9.png[/img]

También, como extra, os compartimos unas capturas de como sería el mapa sin color, para que los más interesados puedan visualizar la geometría de la malla :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/ea66e1bab9049b1a6d6c935a4fdd98f65e1ca0e6.png[/img]

¡Pronto tendréis más noticias del desarrollo de Deck RX! ¡Recuerda añadirlo a tu lista de deseados [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1529180/Deck_RX_The_Deckbuilding_Racing_Game/]aquí[/url] y recomiéndaselo a un amigo si crees que le puede interesar! ¡Eso nos ayuda mucho a llegar a más gente!

¡Nos vemos pronto!

notes.title: New dialogues!
notes.notes:
Hello once again!

Today we are here to show you one of the many changes we are making in [b]Deck RX[/b] thanks to your feedback!

A lot of people have said that they were kind of annoyed by the dialogue frames that appeared after certain actions within a race such as duels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/32325b99d24419fa59d7dc699bd905577bb1d491.jpg[/img]

We decided to introduce these new ones into the game, which are not only smaller but as you can see in the video below they let you know more precisely which vehicles are involved in the action and where they are at that moment.

Also, as you may see, they adapt to the camera position and movement.

[previewyoutube=uiA5Py-0yfo;full][/previewyoutube]

We have taken into account the priority of the information that interests the player, being this

[b]ACTION > VEHICLES INVOLVED > CAPTION. [/b]

This along with other changes will be coming to versions like the demo or the Open Dev Access that our Kickstarter backers have soon.

Tell us what you think about this change!

See you soon!

notes.title: Bordeaux redesign
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

We are introducing you the new design of one of[b] Deck RX[/b]’s main characters, Bordeaux.

We are working on visual changes, mainly focused on the interface and visual clarity issues of the game, trying to make the game [b]easier to understand[/b]. We will be showing more of these changes in the following weeks but now, we will show you the visual rework of this character.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/eb6f3213ef1383ea21f0ec1fca72e283d120aead.gif[/img]

This is the new version of [b]Bordeaux[/b]. We have made a complete redesign of the character to fit the look that we want for Deck RX. We have even added an animated metallic tail that we think gives personality to the character design.

We've also decided to change her entire look as well as her face, but we decided to keep her colors, as her ship – at least for now – remains the same. Oh yes, and she's missing an arm. She was too much powerful with two.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/863b1d8351917a9e18195388c5596a71b21fb3df.gif[/img]

I said she was too strong with two because Bordeaux is still [b]the deadliest racer of the Deck Races![/b]

Here you can see a small tease of one of her cards. This one in particular makes impossible for the enemies to overtake her ship without starting a fight! Thanks to these exclusive cards that each character has, Bordeaux has a very characteristic fighting mechanics, being able to take advantage even when she's losing duels. Bordeaux can also vary the amount of hp enemies lose after receiving damage from a lost clash, so don't be surprised if you win the race by eliminating all your competitors!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/d609af20a74729759345c0a2fdf5469f5bf21e44.png[/img]


We keep working every time we can on [b]Deck RX[/b], we have a lot of features and ideas and we are trying to implement them in the main game in a coherent way. Soon we will talk about a redesign we are working on for the [b]Steam capsules and store presence![/b] And maybe sooner than you think we will announce a new character... Stay tuned!

Remember you can follow the[b] Deck RX[/b] development by following us on our [b][url=https://twitter.com/meteorbyte_stu]Twitter[/url][/b], joining our [url=https://discord.com/invite/895vmPBsKx][b]Discord[/b][/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1529180/Deck_RX_The_Deckbuilding_Racing_Game/][b]wishlisting the game[/b][/url]!

Thank you all for reading, see you soon!

notes.title: Unfortunately, Deck RX will be delayed to 2023.
notes.notes:
Hello! I hope this update finds you well.


It has been a while without updating you on how the [b]Deck RX [/b]project is going and today, we finally bring you some news. The superbackers that are part of the Open Dev Access have more info on this topic as we talk to them from time to time on [url=https://discord.gg/895vmPBsKx]Discord[/url] about how the development is going. Feel free to join!

A Kickstarter campaign, although successful, with a total amount of 10.000€ like ours does not allow us to complete in its entirety the ambitious project we have in hand. And above all, we don't want to deliver a bad or unfinished product. We want to do things right and even if it takes us more time, [b]even if it hurts us, we prefer to tell publicly that Deck RX will be delayed from Q4 2022 to 2023.[/b]

We made this decision because as some of you may know we are also Publishers for other studios, helping them to bring their games to the public both PC and major consoles.

We have already published [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1550740/Ignited_Steel_Mech_Tactics/]Ignited Steel[/url], on March and it will soon receive an update and will be ported to consoles. Also, we are currently working on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1961260/Running_on_Magic/]Running on Magic[/url], which is now available both on PC and consoles.

We are also working on[b] commissions and collaborations[/b] that we are not allowed to announce yet but they will be revealed in the following months. We support our studio with these, allowing us to survive and keep making our own games on our spare time. Unfortunately, we have been especially busy these past few months.

As I was saying, we are forced to delay the release of Deck RX as well as its beta for backers with this reward tier just for a few months. We believe it is better to delay it and deliver a product that best resembles our intention with the game. We rather prefer this than launch the game on an incomplete state pretending it is in its final form.

We can show you that we are still working on [b]Deck RX[/b] as soon as we can free up a few more weeks. A large update is underway, with a new [b]pilot[/b], new[b] cards[/b], a new world, a new [b]enemy[/b], and a whole new [b]“inventory”[/b] system where you can equip parts on each car. Here's a[b] video[/b] of a new map (with its special mechanic included and functional, though not with the final game's look) and a new character that is already in the game, [b]Rusty.[/b]

[previewyoutube=fJozx4N9Mwc;full][/previewyoutube]


We will keep informing about the progress of Deck RX both here and in our[url=https://twitter.com/meteorbyte_stu] Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.gg/895vmPBsKx]Discord.[/url]

We hope you all are staying safe and fine, big greetings from all the Meteorbyte team!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/69d920518e2e94f7ce570c94ddc96b4a61bca2b3.png[/img]

notes.title: We've changed...
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

After a few weeks, I’m once again here to show you what we’ve been working on for [b]Deck RX[/b] but this time, it doesn't affect the content of the game although it's a really important change. We’ve changed the [b]main logo[/b] of the title. We’ve been considering this for a long time now and we think it fits really well with the title because after almost two years of development we now know a lot more about [b]Deck RX[/b] in comparison to when we first designed the logo.

We’ve made this decision to give the title a different style and show how we really want the game to look like. Here’s a comparison between[b] old[/b] and [b]new[/b] logo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/ca7f2de15363e6cfc3d8c6217fedb2e612379782.png[/img]

As you can see, the new logo is more simple and minimalist. We really think that the old one, even when it was more colorful and strong, didnt fit too well with the Deck RX aesthetic and it was less versatile. With the new one we seek contrast, combining it with the new main capsule design for the Steam store page. We also changed the subtitle [b]"The deckbuilding racing game"[/b] for [b]"Racing deckbuilding"[/b] simplifying the concept.

Vertical Capsule:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/70e43cb10d36de7a57fc5690645e2c5fbfed1461.png[/img]

Small Capsule:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/06e043cc0f357bbd5c2f8e63972cabafc6f3e5e8.png[/img]

We’ve been studying similar capsules from deckbuilding titles to give[b] Deck RX[/b] our own outer space/sci-fi style. Finally we chose [b]Locust KV.26[/b] stalking in a cosmic background accompained with the new logo.

This does not mean we got rid of the old logo, we are on a transition period right in the middle of the [b]Deck RX[/b] development and this goes with both in and out-of-game aspects of the title. We are just trying what works and what does not. We just want the best for the game.

For example, do you think the [b]Deck RX[/b] Kickstarter would have gone better with this new logo? We will never know but share your thoughts down below! We are reading you!

Hope this update finds you well and see you soon!

notes.title: Deck RX development after Kickstarter
notes.notes:
Hi again! Hope you are all doing well!

After the Deck RX Kickstarter, we’ve been working on several things related to the game and its development. As you may know, one of the rewards of the campaign was the Open Dev Access, this allows you to play an updatable demo in which we would add content that will be in the final game. First thing we developed was characters, playable and non playable ones, which will be used as enemies.

First, we gave live to Oraklos, the Deaf City’s special enemy. After this, we created Bordeaux, a playable character that is already part of Deck RX, and this time you are able to play as her! Now, the Open Dev Access Superbackers have a new character to race with! Bordeaux is a duel-related character and she’s focused on constantly fighting her enemies, check this video we’ve created for her release!

[previewyoutube=FSLFX61yQUY;full][/previewyoutube]

We are also working on other aspects of the game such as map variety.

Both in the free demo and in the open dev access, even when there are different racetracks, they are all within the same location so we are also developing a new map that will include new mechanics and circuits that do not appear in Deaf City. We already announced the second location of the game but now we have at least one racetrack prototype that we are able to show you as the new Deck RX environment! Its called The Wastesands (this name is still provisional)

[previewyoutube=ZE5GykZL360;full][/previewyoutube]

And for the rest of the rewards, we are delivering them as fast as we can, we are a small studio and we don't have all the resources we would like but we are going slow and steady with it.

We will be giving more info about the Deck RX development in the coming weeks!

Thank you for reading and see you soon!

notes.title: Demo 03 is up!
notes.notes:
Hiya!

New demo for Deck RX (version 03) has been released! This will be the game's stable demo for a long, long time.

Here is a comprehensive changelog for the demo:

## [0.1.5] - Demo_03 - 2021.12.24

### Added
	- Pressing "Shift + Q" or "Shift + E" will now make the camera perform
	a fast rotation of 90 degrees.
	- Panning and rotating camera with mouse buttons.
	- Highlight effect on player car during its turn.
	- Car panels are highlightable during character's Zero Effect choice 
	phase at the start of the race.

### Changed
	- Replaced dropdowns by choosers in game speed mode and graphics mode
	entries in the settings menu.
	- Car names in Race Finish screen are now tinted with their main car color.
	- Rework in minimized car panels' color scheme.
	- Car panels better reflect car deaths.
    
### Fixed
    - Issue which would prevent changing game speed mode and graphics mode when
    the settings menu opens during a race.
	- Pause menu no longer shows when pressing "Escape" to close an expanded
	view of the card piles during a race.
	- Bug where some enemies would start the race before the player in rare
	occasions.
	- The turn counter icon in the car panel is hidden once the car dies.
	- Lighting artefacts in Deaf City solar panel props.
	- Occassional memory access issues provoked by the destruction of track props 
	and buildings after track tiles break off during explosions.

### Removed
	- UI elements making a call to action to the Kickstarter campaign.
	- Settings menu no longer displays the high-fidelity graphics quality option.



Those of you who have participated on the Kickstarter with Gold pledges or higher will have received an email with your test key for the Open Development Build. The first version of this build is now live as well! Check our Discord for more info on this update's features!

Thanks everyone for helping us make Deck RX a reality!

Happy holidays!

- The Meteorbyte Team

notes.title: Introducing Bordeaux, our new playable character
notes.notes:
Last week we showed you this image and promised you more info coming this week news, well, [b]here we are again[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/ddf9bfc4461f45c90c9f728254ca6d3d989992bc.png[/img]

We officially announce [b]Bordeaux[/b], the first playable character that we will add to [b]Deck RX[/b] in an upcoming update. As you may know, backers with the [b]Open Dev Access Pass[/b] (Gold and above) will be the first to be able to ride the [b]Deck Races[/b] with her.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/c7f93e878f0c553c30582707a10c2f929ec5eb07.gif[/img]

Some of you may already know this, but [b]Bordeaux[/b] is a duel-based character that takes advantage of [b]aggressive decks[/b]. She is interested in initiating duels with her enemies, as she will have dueling related mechanics to get [b]special benefits[/b] thanks to her unique cards, such as [b]restoring life after a duel, double damage...[/b] or even gaining advantage from[b] lost clash[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/a475244c380dabe9df547b3ef34e85f0c692c2cb.gif[/img]

[b]Bordeaux[/b] will ride the [b]Scarlet Widow,[/b] as you can see, our artists gave her a design as aggressive as she is. Sharp, pointed shapes to confront her enemies. Aggresive colors because she doesnt need to hide from their enemies, their enemies should fear her.

[b]Bordeaux is a born hunter.[/b]

We remind you that if you want to enjoy the new features that [b]Bordeaux[/b] will bring to [b]Deck RX[/b], you can have access to this content and more before anyone else with the [b]Open Dev Access pass[/b] (Gold tier and above)

The Kickstarter campaign for [b]Deck RX[/b] is about to end and we need your support more than ever! Go tell your friends and family that an amaizing deckbuilder is on developing and they are looking for fundings to launch an incredible game! 


Thank you all for reading and see you soon!

notes.title: Upcoming map for Deck RX!
notes.notes:
Today we officially announce the second map of Deck RX,[b] The Wastesands[/b] [i](Temporary name)[/i]

[b]The Wastesands[/b] will be the second map available for the [b]Deck RX[/b] demo and backers who have [b]Open Dev Access[/b] as a reward in their pledge tiers [b](Gold and above)[/b] will be able to ride this map soon. Here you have an early render of the map’s background as a [b]3D concept[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/302e5d706982811c6ecc2d19c020cd664bf0eb10.gif[/img]

[b]The Wastesands[/b] is a desertic industrial area far away from the solar system, desolated by high temperatures and full of tunnels through which the race will take place. These tunnels will be the special mechanic of this second map (just as the mines will be in[b] Deaf City[/b] after the release of [b]Oraklos[/b]). In these tunnels you will have no vision of your pilot or surroundings. Just like you, the enemies will also lose their sight... all except one, the special enemy for [b]The Wastesands[/b] (which is in development) that will anchor itself to the tunnel walls ready to ambush the racers that are approaching.

Some of you may have already seen the design of this map, our lead artist Ulises developed part of it livestreaming on his twitch channel. And those of you who haven't seen it there... maybe those ancient giant mech scraps…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/acbdcd3efd4cf2ba867a89827486ce32ba62f739.gif[/img]

As I said, this will officially become part of [b]Deck RX[/b] in the next weeks and backers with [b]Open Dev Access[/b] will be the first players to ride the second map of the Deck RX adventure!

So... why not consider increasing your pledge? Nah, just kidding… [i][b]unless...[/b][/i]

Thank you guys for all the love you show to the [b]Deck RX[/b] campaign. We have already passed the 50% of the total goal and we are so happy with how things are going with [b]Deck RX![/b]

Stay tuned for upcoming updates and thanks for reading!

See you soon!

notes.title: Introducing a new enemy for Deck RX!
notes.notes:
Hi guys! I'm here to talk about a new enemy we are introducing into Deck RX!

Oraklos are a coven of techno-priestesses who have been modified and trained since birth at the Temple-Labs, making them able to break the barriers of the mind and take their vision beyond what any human can reach, across the vastness of space-time. They are expert mind-readers, often employed by Deaf City’s government. Since the Cult of the True Way is pursuing immortality, they have decided to yield some of their best agents to this enterprise by enrolling them in the Deck Race. Like most other enemies, Oraklos come in 3 different tiers of strength, depending on how late in the game you encounter them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/fd2ae719c12dfe91e15ef8f02f42c51b7ea8a3c1.gif[/img]

With Oraklos, we introduce a world-specific enemy to Deaf City. As we mentioned in the Kickstarter, each stage will have both special tiles and hazards, and its own special enemy. Oraklos will drive aggressively, using all types of mines against their enemies - in their deck they will have stasis, hellfire and explosive mines - and they will differentiate situations in the race to know which one to lay down each time.

But... What if you use mines against them? Well, Oraklos can have visions of their future encounters, and are thus extraordinarily capable of dodging mines and adjust their speed accordingly in almost every situation. You’ll be hard pressed to beat them at their own game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/4e93e083ca61301c1c2445ce36738713a6701b9b.gif[/img]

Oraklos’ behavior within the race will change depending on how much health they have. If they are low on health, they will suspend their ship in Stasis, and perform some mild nano-repairs. But if they get ahead of the rest of the racers, they’ll lay mines – MANY mines, so stay alert and plan your turns carefully! Using their visions, Oraklos will have the ability to use both “Evade” and “Drift” to avoid the most of the damage they may suffer while low on health.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/f284c1d02cbf6fa747176414075875aa0988b319.png[/img]

The visual design of Oraklos has been developed from concepts like this one. It has a more elaborate design than regular enemies, and we hope that it contributes to make Deaf City the “Mine World”, where the player must learn that no speed level is safe – driving too fast will make you take damage on curves, but drive too slow… and those mines will end you!

Oraklos-type enemies will be featured in the full version of Deck RX, among other additions which we will reveal in the coming days.

Our Gold-tier backers in Kickstarter (and above) will be able to play against them in-game as early as December 2021, as part of the Open Development Access pass.

Thank you very much for your support so far!

See you soon!

notes.title: Devlog#5: How we use Steam Reviews to change Game Design in DeckRX
notes.notes:
Hi again guys!

This week’s blog has arrived later than usual, but for good reasons that we hope we can detail in a couple months.

[b]So last time we described [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1529180/view/5660440217697976664]the game’s art progression[/url][/b]. Check it out if you haven’t had the chance, there’s been a lot of progression even though DeckRX has been in development only for a couple of months.

[b]This week we’ll describe a couple focus points of our game design (by the way, have you added DeckRX to your wishlist?)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/6ed055f18ca8ca7586707fb555e1af72dceaa00c.png[/img]

We currently have an [b]ambitious vision[/b] of what DeckRX “The Deckbuilding Racing Game” can be. Before describing this vision, we first have to explain a couple key elements of our game design process.

We’re [b]deckbuilding and board gaming fans[/b] “[i]desde chiquititos[/i]” Previous to designing DeckRX we knew which were the weaknesses of games in the genre. Even though [b]deckbuilding games[/b] are pretty common and new ones are released every couple weeks, [b]many have common errors[/b]. You don’t have to play deckbuilding games to see these errors, just head to the[b] Steam Reviews[/b] of popular deckbuilding games. The most frequent complaints are [b]lack of combos[/b], and [b]only one viable deck[/b] if you wish to defeat the game.

We too have suffered these issues when playing deckbuilding games. It’s quite frustrating when you’re playing the early stages of a run in any deckbuilding game, and you already know it might be doomed due to the cards you’ve been delt. Once you reach the boss a couple times, you know there might be only one viable deck for your character, so you restart the run until you get the cards you want.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/c02875d204b6c0853f44910ab61dfe635ce91ab4.png[/img]

We know this is a common problem so we’ll prepare in advance of DeckRX release. Our plan is to [b]create multiple viable decks, increasing the game’s variety and replaybility. Every driver will have its own unique gameplay[/b], and will have multiple viable strategies to beat the tournament. We’re currently brain storming different ways a player can interact with a character. Imagine something like FTL. If you get a certain achievement, you get a slightly different ship which will modify the ship’s gameplay.

Analyzing famous deckbuilding games’ Steam reviews, you see players [b]complain about the lackluster number of combos to play[/b]. On many cases developers design cards individually. They don’t have in mind possible future combinations and explanations. Will make sure [b]DeckRX’s cards are developed holistically, creating multiple strategic possibilities depending on how cards combine with each other.[/b]

How are we going to achieve this? Well, lots of brainstorming and game testing. but [b]we’re not waiting for the game’s prototype to be ready to playtest and balance it![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/088c8ab4d8efcaf291426c537c922fb19ec08343.jpg[/img]

First, [b]we’re developing a card and paper version of the game with all the necessary data printed on it.[/b] We’ll design the tile-circuits on paper and create small tokens representing each of the drivers. We’ll play the game and balance where needed. Who knows, maybe in the[b] future if the game’s successful we’ll release a boardgame version of DeckRX: The Deckbuilding Racing Game.
[/b]
Even though we’re testing the game before it’s release, [b]we still need a lot of help balancing.[/b] DeckRX will be pretty solid, but several dozen pair of eyes are better than 6! If you want to [b]participate in DeckRX’s betatesting phase[/b] (once we have a playable prototype)[b] please head towards our [url=https://discord.gg/invite/mbs]Discord Server[/url] as we’ll be looking for betatesters[/b] among our community.

Well, that’s it for the day! This is not the last time you’ll read a blog related to DeckRX’s game design and how we’re planning to resolve each issue. We’re planning on carrying out a pretty open development.

See you next time!

notes.title: Devlog #4: Art Style progression
notes.notes:
Hi again guys, another week, another blog!

Last week we spoke about [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1529180/view/3079876894666106926][b]who are we and what each of us do as part of the team.[/b][/url]

Today we’re [b]diving deeper into both PJ’s and Ulises’ work[/b]! [url=https://twitter.com/_thisIsPJ]PJ’s[/url] the studio [b]technical artist[/b] while [url=https://twitter.com/RataUnderground]Ulises’[/url] the studio [b]Head of Art[/b], but at the beginning of DeckRX’s development they were not the ones drawing and modelling.

[b]For the first couple of months, we planned that DeckRX would only have a couple of 3D elements.[/b] Of course, you’re thinking “top-down 2D racing, kinda of meh” but no wait… we actually had a kind of a cool idea.

DeckRX development started with the pandemic , [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1529180/view/3059609427967688760]but we already talked about this in the past[/url] . As the game was only being developed by [b]Phil [/b](the studio’s director and one of its programmers) decided for what the industry calls “programmer art” Do you see anything weird in the following images?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/4a9794f1f37b63a55c65563c580fa0396c987a13.jpg[/img]


[b]The ships you’re seeing here are actually 2D![/b]

We used the [i]“sprite stacking”[/i] technique where you…stack…multiple 2D sprites to create a 3D effect. For programmers who aren’t really adept in 3D modelling, it’s a really useful and efficient tool for creating appealing art.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/7e8c620319cc7915e6acc7d42c4094160cf87da1.jpg[/img]

At this moment we decided that [b]the game would mix 2D and 3D elements[/b]. Both the environment and circuits (with all its props and eye-candy) would be modelled and developed in 3D. However, [b]Pixel-art[/b] was used to develop each individual sprite on each ship. We had to make sure that the pixel art and 3D style chosen would mix harmoniously.

We went for a [b]“low-poly”[/b] as it would mix perfectly with the cyberpunk aesthetic we are going for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/8d45547c05d284d926ff43fc47f524c0c8a87bac.gif[/img]

At this stage, there was minimal work in shaders. We briefly started working on shaders and lightning before we decided to rework DeckRX’s artistic style. We haven’t saved many images of this stage of production, where the ships had lighting and shaders implemented.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/b3738936a88632ec44fe277a9c7daf8ab8ea9e24.png[/img]

[i]Don’t really think much of the image to the left, we were using many placeholder images as we were aiming for functionality rather than polish at this time.[/i]

[b]Soon into development we decided to experiment with the artistic style[/b] and see what looked cooler and worked best.[b] We developed a 3D model of one of the ships and measuring how long its development took.[/b] We put in some lighting and shader elbow grease and measured the results. As days went by and we realized the potential DeckRX had, we quickly decided to invest more resources on DeckRX and develop all elements in 3D.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/86ac8fb87b5524357fcb1a9abbc68117c2173b0e.gif[/img]

[u]Background[/u]

You might have observed a big change as time passed in the images we’ve shown. The environment has evolved a lot along the way. We knew the first world would be a cyberpunk’esque city, but we wanted to give it our own style.

Our first try was a bit too much.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/19c1c23a465c6b61fc7bb3cca98af1c39fd8745b.png[/img]

We went for a s[b]tyle reminiscent of old arcade games[/b] which would be mix well with pixel art cars. [b]We iterated several times as we were not happy with the result. [/b]We felt the city and circuit were not harmonizing correctly and felt that we could deliver much more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/bba4f02aa15b56589dea1c0d1e7f0ae3851d28b7.png[/img]

[b]We soon experimented with the cities lighting[/b]. Cyberpunk cities are more recognizable at night, when the city lights and advertising screens are most visible. [b]Now it started looking really good and some wallpapers were being saved.[/b] PJ was happier and happier with his work. Still it was not as good as we could get it to be.

We wanted to give it that purple aesthetic you can sometimes see in [b]Blade Runner[/b]. Cities with individual lightning. The building were also not up with what we believed was a cyberpunk city. Everything was too square. So we began remodelling the city.

[b]Our main objective was to increase the cyberpunk aesthetic[/b]. The city had to be more cluttered, with less repetition and an improved lighting. Less height uniformity was necessary, as well as some dynamic movement. A screen should never be static.

We focused on [b]three different elements[/b] that would add dynamism to the world:

[list]
[*] Buildings with flickering lights
[*] Small ships going from one building to another
[*] Fog covering the city and transitioning along the map
[/list]

[b]Before adding these elements to DeckRX we had to make sure they wouldn't disrupt general gameplay.[/b] We need to maintain player focus on the gameplay itself. We don’t players focusing on small ships going from one place to another when there’s a whole race taking place.

[previewyoutube=n-GKMu617D0;full][/previewyoutube]

Well now that this blog is done, and we have described the artistic style we are approaching,[b] what can you expect in future blogs?[/b]

[b]We didn’t discuss much on character concept art[/b] (I just dropped down this topic for future blogs) For now[b] we have only conceptualized 2 drivers[/b] each with their own mechanics, art style and personality so much work is left in this area, but we can still discuss what we’re going for. We have already several concepts prepared for the rest of the drivers that we’re prepared to show.

As we have mentioned previously, [b]they’re going to be several different planets in which to race in. Each planet will have its own personality and mechanics[/b], something we’re still conceptualizing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/088c8ab4d8efcaf291426c537c922fb19ec08343.jpg[/img]

Well that it’s for the day! As always, remember you can[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1529180/view/3059609427967688760] wishlist the game on Steam[/url], and join our community on [url=https://discord.com/invite/mbs]Discord [/url]if you want to discuss anything with us.

See you space cowboy...

notes.title: Devlog #3: The team behind DeckRX: The Deckbuilding Racing Game
notes.notes:
Hi guys, how you doin’ this week? New week, new blog so let’s get things going.[b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1529180/view/3059609427967688760] Last week[/url][/b] we spoke about how we first conceptualized DeckRX.

This week [b]we’ll speak a bit more about the team[/b] behind the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1529180/Deck_RX_The_Deckbuilding_Racing_Game/]“DeckRX: The Deckbuilding Racing Game”[/url] development, [b]who we are and what each one of us do.[/b]

[b]The studio was born back in 2017[/b]. After “Ludum Dare #36” we decided to turn our jam into a full game.[b] At that time the studio consisted of a coder/founder and an artist[/b]. Almost 2 years later we launched [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/878420/Woodpunk/]WOODPUNK [/url]on Steam. When WOODPUNK launched, the studio had grown to 4 members: two programmers, an artist, and a marketing specialist.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/2a9cc6d81b893747c29e564a77884d5ea49ef72c.png[/img]
[h3][i]"Hi, we’re Meteorbyte Studios. You may remember us from famous roguelike shooter “WOODPUNK”[/i][/h3]

[b]Not much later we started conceptualizing “Attrah”[/b], one of our main projects which we've been developing on and off ever since. As this is one of our most ambitious projects yet, we need a whole lot of funding. [b]We decided to branch out by becoming an indie publisher and developing smaller games on the side[/b]. The whole [b]COVID [/b]thing “helped” us carry this decision forward and soon [b]DeckRX was born[/b].

For most of the Studio’s life, the team consisted on 4 core members, but we recently grew to 5 members plus some people helping us out!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/39da5f03a15881f85cf8cc9a17867de2fbcafdda.png[/img]
[b]Phil’s the studio’s founder[/b]. He’s the director and (much to his demise) codes whenever he has time. [b]He’s the mind behind DeckRX’s conception[/b]. He’s a big tabletop fan, but war games is where it’s at (not those casual party games) He has more than a thousand hours into Europa Universalis IV.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/dcde18c6ba1f18bd75adb8a70a4607991a47e2b8.png[/img]

[b][url=https://twitter.com/RataUnderground]Ulises’s[/url] the studio’s lead artist.[/b] Before dwelling in the gamedev industry, he was and still is a[b] comic illustrator[/b]. He’s most recent and biggest comics are [url=http://www.uliseslafuente.com/art88-46/index.asp]ART88/46[/url] and [url=http://fandogamia.com/fanternet/comic/stageone/607/race-01]Stage One[/url]. He’s the one behind DeckRX 3D-modelling and character Design.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/0c180b80269233b44c78c69808f84af425469fed.png[/img]
[b][url=https://twitter.com/_thisIsPJ]PJ’s [/url]a software developer and technical artist[/b]. He’s also a [b]solo-dev[/b], recently released [b][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=--6uBzBQ6n8]Roguecube[/url][/b]. He’s extremely proud of how DECKRX’s looking like, as he’s the one in charge of [b]shaders and lightning[/b] and all of that kind of stuff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/2064354a7efcf4d03c69a7f8363b5e1677cf59db.png[/img]
[url=https://twitter.com/inmamlobo]Inma’s [/url]the studio newest member. [b]She’s both in the art and coding department[/b]. She’s a [b]software engineer with a passion for illustration[/b]. She’s the one in charge of most of the card illustrations you see. She's also a solo dev for an unnanounced project!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/ab96a839307d0981f51a2fa545aec7072d2c679c.png[/img]
[b][url=https://twitter.com/sans_juniour]Santi [/url][/b](the guy typing this) is [b]the studio’s marketing guy[/b]. I’m the [b]PE teacher of the video game industry[/b]. I don’t know how to code, and I’m shit at drawing, but I still want to make some games.

[b]Oscar and David[/b] are also currently helping us out in coding and art respectively!

[b]So, what can you expect from each one of us in the following months?[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/faf615830326b66370b02259895fc1610c4ca32b.jpg[/img]
So much work. [b]Phil [/b]will be busy directing the studio and designing the game (a process which every member in the studio puts in their cent, even the marketing guy) [b]Ulises [/b]will be modelling and conceptualizing all of the game’s drivers/pilots, while [b]Inma [/b]designs all future card illustration. I in the other hand will be preparing blogs, a Kickstarter campaign and communicating with you guys. [b]Head on to our [url=https://discord.com/invite/mbs]Discord [/url]if you want to chat with us!
[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/c1e4927f0eda51a4b4a6297e716f48502e03c2f9.jpg[/img]
Well, that’s it for the week! It has been short but intense. [b]Now that the introductions are out of the way, in the next couple weeks[/b] we’ll dive deeper into the game itself. We’ll describe different elements related to DeckRX, like how development is going, concept art, and the features that make DeckRX unique.

[b]‘Til next week![/b]

notes.title: Dev-log Announcement!
notes.notes:
Hi guys! 
For the next months we'll be carrying out a [b]devlog describing different elements of DeckRX: The Deckbuilding Racing Game development[/b]. New articles will come out weekly / bi-weekly depending on the workload.
If at any time you have a question, just let us a comment at the end of the article, or join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/mbs]Discord [/url](we'll answer much faster!)

Enjoy!

So, let’s get to this week’s blog! In the following paragraphs we’re describing where and[b] how the idea of DeckRX was born, and how DeckRX’s theme[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/4a9794f1f37b63a55c65563c580fa0396c987a13.jpg[/img]
[i]See something weird here? We’ll go over it in the following blogs[/i]

[b]DeckRX was conceived in the middle of the pandemic.[/b] The global economic situation caused an extensive change in our business model. Suddenly we couldn’t travel to those events where we would have met future investors and secure funding. We decided to c[b]hange our approach to gamedev[/b] in the short run. For the following months we would be developing smaller, [b]more direct to market products[/b]. That way we can fund our more ambitious project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/ada93a3917428d8cac3426173003c8012f09be10.jpg[/img]

[i]Playing with different versions of the logo once we found the name for the game
[/i]

As most of the greatest ideas come to mind… in the shower (not the toilet) the studio’s director thought… [b]“there aren’t any deckbuilding racing games”[/b] He had been playing [b]“Slay The Spire”[/b] for the last weeks and analyzed the different approaches to the deckbuilding genre. After the success of “Slayer the Spire” a whole bunch of deckbuilding games were published. Most of them are RPGs, with the odd one out here and there. Loving the genre, and knowing that it’s current fad, we decided to create a new approach to the deckbuilding genre.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/da26d0562a283a5f4bb81cc6c6aca3af18d3e006.jpg[/img]

[b]We’re big table top fans[/b]. The board gaming market has several different approaches to the deckbuilding genre, but the video game market doesn’t! We got some inspiration here and there from other tabletop deckbuilding games. Even though we haven’t played it, our community has mentioned the similarities we have to “Flamme Rouge”

So, the idea was born. A deckbuilding, combat racing game. Sounds cool. How is it going to be, western “mad max” style or something else? Well…there hasn’t been a F-Zero game for a while now…


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/83f0bf86865266390f21de32517102ef1b3080a1.jpg[/img]

We’re big fans of[b] F-Zero GX[/b], so why not do a card game slightly inspired by it?

Then we have it! [b]A deckbuilding racing game influenced by F-Zero games. We’ll have cyberpunk cities, the guitar riffs, awesome cars (or ships?), and pilots (drivers?)
[/b]
Are their any other influences? Sure. We’re the kind of people who love to put little references to the things we love all around our games. I’m pretty sure you’ll be able to see references to retro video games, anime, and pop culture here and there here and there. I can promise you’ll definitely find references Formula 1 memes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40322498/a9ea283a993cbaa336f64d796e86c1f18e7a2f55.gif[/img]

Well that's it for today!

If you wish to get the latest news on DeckRX [url=https://discord.com/invite/mbs]Join our Discord Community[/url]!
